deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This controls whether terraform can delete the resource. Setting it to PREVENT or ABANDON can help avoid accidental deletion of critical routing policies, which could disrupt network traffic and security.

name.description: Name of the route policy. This policy's name, which must be a resource ID segment and unique within all policies owned by the Router
name.rationale: The resource name is only used to identify the route policy and does not affect its security or behaviour.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies the Google Cloud project where the resource is created. It determines resource placement but does not directly affect the security configuration of the route policy.

region.description: Region where the router and NAT reside.
region.rationale: Determines the region where the resource is created. Restricting deployment to approved regions helps meet organisational and regulatory data residency requirements.

router.description: The name of the Cloud Router in which this route policy will be configured.
router.rationale: References the Cloud Router where the policy is attached. It identifies the target resource but does not directly introduce a security risk

type.description: This is policy's type, which is one of IMPORT or EXPORT Possible values: ["ROUTE_POLICY_TYPE_IMPORT", "ROUTE_POLICY_TYPE_EXPORT"]
type.rationale: Determines the functional type of the route policy (import or export). It does not directly affect security but influences how routes are processed.

terms.description: List of terms (the order in the list is not important, they are evaluated in order of priority).

terms.priority.description: The evaluation priority for this term, which must be between 0 (inclusive) and 2147483648 (exclusive), and unique within the list.
terms.priority.rationale: controls the evaluation order of policy trerms. It does not directly affect security but determines which term is applied first when multiple terms match.

terms.actions.description: 'CEL expressions to evaluate to modify a route when this term matches.'\

terms.actions.description.rationale: Provides a human-readable description of the action and does not affect how the policy is enforced.

terms.actions.expression.description:
Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression
Language syntax.
terms.actions.expression.rationale: Defines the action to be taken when the term matches. While it influences route modification, it does not inherently introduce a security risk unless misconfigured.

terms.actions.location.description:
String indicating the location of the expression for error
reporting, e.g. a file name and a position in the file
terms.actions.location.rationale: Used only for error reporting and debugging. It does not affect policy behaviour or security.

terms.actions.title.description:
Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its
purpose.
terms.actions.title.rationale: Provides a descriptive title for the action. It is informational only and has no impact on security.

terms.match.description: CEL expression evaluated against a route to determine if this term applies (see Policy Language).

terms.match.description.rationale: Provides documentation for the matching condition and does not influence policy evaluation.

terms.match.expression.description: Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.
terms.match.expression.rationale: Defines the condition under which the term applies. While it determines when actions are executed, it does not inherently introduce a security risk unless misconfigured.

terms.match.location.description: String indicating the location of the expression for error reporting, e.g. a file name and a position in the file
terms.match.location.rationale: Used only for error reporting and debugging. It does not affect the behaviour or security of the route policy.

terms.match.title.description: Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its purpose.
terms.match.title.rationale: Provides a descriptive title for the matching condition and has no effect on policy behaviour or security.
